items_missed: No full agenda statement - asked 'is now a good time to ask you some questions?' but never laid out the roadmap (gather details, then walk through pricing) or the 10-15 minute timeframe
Never explicitly checked/confirmed availability for the Sept 1 date - only asked 'were you still looking for that Tuesday?'
Never got the destination address or zip code - quoted a move without knowing where it was going
No probe on additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), storage stops, or additional stops
No access concerns asked at either location - parking, walk distance, elevator, HOA/gate restrictions
No moving-stressor question, despite the customer volunteering she is moving her 86-year-old mother with two medical beds - a clear emotional cue left unexplored
No 'pricing is super simple' opener
Never stated the hourly rate, the per-mover-per-hour structure, or the crew size - only gave flat dollar totals ($760 and $570)
No No Worries Damage Coverage mention ($2,000 accidental damage) and no 60 cents/lb baseline - zero insurance content on the entire call
No Meet Your Mover pitch
No On-Time Guarantee pitch
No 'no hidden fees' pitch - no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no transportation or assembly fees
Entire Clock section skipped - no clock-starts-on-site, no 2.5 hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check
Never stated number of movers or trucks on the estimate
Never explained walk distance or drive time as variables that move the number
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped - no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip
No deposit never mentioned - the single easiest objection-remover, and the customer was actively deciding whether to book
Offered 'do you want me to make the reservation, or just send over the email?' - gave the customer an easy out instead of asking for the booking
Never explained what is in the confirmation email - no bolded detail list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?'
top_strength: Excellent use of the customer's history - he pulled the previous contract live on the call, named the prior crew (Tyler), and anchored the estimate to what the move actually took last time (3 hours) rather than a generic guess. Then he priced both the 3-hour and 4-hour scenarios out loud with an explicit hour of wiggle room, which is honest, budget-conscious framing that let her pick a number she believed.
coaching_note: Alex built real trust in six minutes and then gave away the booking. When Kendall was ready, he said 'do you want me to go ahead and make the reservation, or do you want me to just send over the email right now?' - that 'or' handed her the exit, and she took it ('send it over, I'll probably call you back'). Ask for the booking as the single option and pair it with 'there's no deposit, so nothing is locked financially - if anything changes we just move it.' On this call, no-deposit alone likely closes it. Second priority: he skipped the entire Clock and differentiator block. Even on a repeat customer, the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments explain why the $570 number is what it is, and No Worries coverage matters more than usual here - two medical beds and an 86-year-old customer's belongings.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and easy - he respected that she was working, referenced her prior crew by name, and matched her on the first-floor comment ('Perfect, perfect, we do too'), and she closed with 'I appreciate you,' though the repeated 'Okay, good deal' filler made some transitions feel like acknowledgment rather than listening.
